audit.why: 46.17% over 1265 games. Lane phase genuinely favours you — he is immobile and Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1 — but the matchup is graded EVEN 5.5/10 because his scaling, not his lane, is the threat.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows disagreed across layers: full read Orianna/Orianna/Skill/Skill at rows 1-4 against content Skill/Skill/Orianna/Orianna, and row 6 read Veigar in the full layer against Orianna in the content layer. The packet also flags the chart as over-crediting Orianna against a 46.17% win rate.
audit.why: Rows 1-4: content and packet agree with each other and with the kit (his 1000-range Q arrives at 2; the cage is up at 3; from 4 he is a stationary target for the pull-back ball). Row 6: Phenomenal Evil grants permanent, uncapped AP and Primordial Burst scales with missing health, so two-plus items is his, not yours — the full layer was right and the content layer wrong, which also moves the chart back toward the recorded win rate.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-4 aligned to the content layer; row 6 aligned the other way by moving win[6] and whys[6] to Veigar to match phases[6].side. Every touched why rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns stated the cage-edge rule but carried no number anywhere.
audit.why: Event Horizon is 20/18.5/17/15.5/14 — the longest punishable cooldown in the lane against your 7s-to-3s Q. Baleful Strike is 6s; Primordial Burst is 120/90/60 and scales with the target's missing health.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 20-second Event Horizon window was never quantified as the step-up cue.
audit.why: It is the single gap that decides the lane: he has no dash and no escape while it is down.
audit.corrected: Stated with the number in breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[1].d.

edits.before: Q-W online: the classic chunk combo. Trade it on his last-hits and keep the ball where his approach must cross it.
edits.after: Baleful Strike poke arrives at 1000 range and the trade war levels off — trade only while his cage is down.

edits.before: E completes the kit: ball-on-self beats his engage, ball-on-wave farms, ball-on-him threatens. The chess match begins.
edits.after: Event Horizon and Dark Matter are both online: a spacing war. Only the cage EDGE stuns — never step through the wall.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q-W every wave contact now. The Dissonance field controls every step he takes near the ball.
edits.after: Shove him in and walk out of the telegraphed Dark Matter — he is immobile, so the ball's pull-back hits him twice.

edits.before: Shockwave online — your lane presence doubles without casting anything. Every wave he contests is a potential flip.
edits.after: Primordial Burst grows on missing health, so stay healthy and tax his immobility — but never step into a fresh cage.

edits.before: Late Ori is the teamfight: protect-ball on your diver, shockwave their clump, and dissonance the choke they retreat through.
edits.after: He out-scales you here: Phenomenal Evil is permanent AP with no cap, so his ceiling climbs every wave and yours does not.

edits.before: In fights your Shockwave outvalues his single cage if you dodge it - yours.
edits.after: Two-plus items go to Veigar - Phenomenal Evil stacks permanently and never caps.

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. Check it before every step-up. - E Command: Protect is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Event Horizon: 20s at rank 1 and 14s maxed — only the cage EDGE stuns, so hold near the centre or leave before it forms and never step through the wall. That 20s gap is your step-up window. - Baleful Strike is 6s. - Primordial Burst is 120s at level 6 and grows on your missing health.

edits.before: From Luden's you run rivers: shove the wave, hover the ball at the choke, and Shockwave the first clump that contests. Protect-ball on your jungler doubles every gank.
edits.after: From Luden's you run rivers: shove the wave, hover the ball at the choke, and Shockwave the first clump that contests. Ball on your jungler adds shield, armour and MR to the dive.

edits.before: Ball on his farm path, Q-W the last-hit contact, auto-weave once, and recall the ball — three-second trades his combo math can't answer.
edits.after: Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1 against your Q's 7s — in that gap land the ball, W through it, and weave a passive auto on his face.

edits.before: Poking with the ball stranded at max range when his engage is up — an Orianna without her ball is a Doran's Ring with legs.
edits.after: Your E is 9s and soaks the Dark Matter hit; your R is 110s and answers a clump. Never spend the 110s escaping one cage.

edits.before: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Luden's Companion into Sorcerer's, then Shadowflame and Rabadon's. Zhonya's vs dive — buy the stopwatch the moment Zed hits 6.
edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Luden's Companion into Sorcerer's, then Shadowflame and Rabadon's. Zhonya's vs dive — buy the stopwatch the moment Veigar hits 6.

notes: The packet carries a defect: 'level chart contradicts data: Orianna wins only 46.17% but the chart gives Orianna 4/7 stages vs 0'. Row 6 was repaired the other direction — win[6] and whys[6] moved to Veigar to match phases[6].side — because Phenomenal Evil is uncapped permanent AP and that is the only kit-grounded reading of a two-plus-item stage; it also reduces the Orianna-favoured count the defect complains about. See questionsForUser: rows 0, 3 and 4 still leave Orianna favoured on three stages in a 46.17% lane and I did not move them without a kit reason.
questionsForUser: Orianna vs Veigar (mid), level chart: after the repairs the chart still reads Orianna at Level 1, Levels 4-5 and Level 6 in a lane Orianna wins only 46.17% of the time (packet flags this as a defect). Rows 4-5 and 6 are kit-defensible (he is immobile, his R needs missing health), so I left them. Do you want those two stages moved to Skill to bring the chart in line with the win rate, or is the chart meant to describe lane tempo rather than game outcome?
